blocks.text: Short-dated government bond yields have eased as traders push back their expectations for rate cuts, yet longer maturities have barely moved. The result is a steeper yield curve driven by the long end, a pattern consistent with a rising term premium.

It is the extra return investors demand to hold a long-dated bond instead of rolling over short-term ones. Heavy government issuance, less predictable inflation and smaller central-bank balance sheets have all pushed it higher.

items: Mortgage and corporate borrowing costs track long yields more than policy rates.
Weak demand at long-dated auctions would reinforce the trend.
A faster disinflation path would be the most likely catalyst for relief.

blocks.text: Even when policy rates fall, financing conditions may stay tighter than borrowers expect. The bond market is, in effect, sharing the work of monetary policy.
